The method supports several functional forms for $\eta_{xyz}(t)$ [S1, unofficial]:

The evidence explicitly lists and defines several functional forms for the learning rate adjustment (referred to as $eta_{xyz}(t)$ in the claim, though the text uses $rw(x)$, $s(t)$, $c(t)$, $l(t)$, and $E(t)$). These include: 1) Two-stage rectangular wave transformation ($rw(x)$), 2) Sine-based change ($s(t)$), 3) Cosine-based change ($c(t)$), 4) Linear learning rate change ($l(t)$), and 5) Exponential learning rate change ($E(t)$). The claim states that the method supports several functional forms, which is directly confirmed by the equations and descriptions provided in Source [S1].
supported
The source does not provide a closed-form solution for deriving these from desired start/end points for the exponential case, only stating it passes through two points [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly defines the exponential learning rate change as $E(t) = ε e^{δ t} + η$ with $ε, δ, η$ as fitting coefficients. It states that this function passes through two points $(t_1, E(t_1))$ and $(t_2, E(t_2))$. It does not provide a closed-form solution for deriving the coefficients $ε, δ, η$ directly from arbitrary start/end points (unlike the linear case which provides a specific equation relating $l(t)$ to points). Therefore, the claim that the source does not provide a closed-form solution for deriving these from desired start/end points, but only states it passes through two points, is supported by the text.
